newsitem.title: UK: Portugal, Greece meet EU's low sulphur diesel specification.
newsitem.headline: Portugal, Greece meet EU's low sulphur diesel specification.

text.p: Portugal should be ready to supply low sulphur diesel to the European market from April, state oil company Petrogal said on Thursday.

When the European Union ruled last year that the sulphur content in diesel would have to be reduced to 0.05 percent from 0.2 percent by October 1, 1996, Portugal and Greece said the timescale was too fast.
Both countries were allowed to delay the introduction -- until January 1997 for Greece and March 1997 for Portugal.
Greece managed to adhere to the January deadline and Portugal's Petrogal says it will also meet the EU extension.
"We will be producing 0.05 percent diesel this month (March), but it won't be on the market until April," one of the group's traders said.

The European Union allowed the temporary deferrals to Portugal and Greece in recognition of the need to install desulphurisation units at refineries and also to allow stocks of existing 0.2 percent sulphur to be used up.
